messages:
anya: ran a focused sim this morning for KV residency skew during long-context workloads. reproduces the memory creep + eviction storms when a cold-start tenant ramps and touches long ctx keys. short summary then raw snippets.

mike: quick TL;DR numbers please? :eyes:

anya: top-line — under our current LRU-ish resident policy:
- tenant-heavy workload can occupy ~65-75% of global KV residency within 5m of ramp
- other tenants see eviction rate spikes x3 and p99 latency jumps for model calls that miss KV
- after sustained long ctx runs, total cached bytes increases ~8% over 30m (we expect stable)

anya: sample profiler dump (trimmed):
```
KV residency by tenant (bytes):
  tenant-alpha: 2.1GB (70% res)
  tenant-beta: 600MB (20% res)
  tenant-gamma: 300MB (10% res)
Eviction events last 60s: 134
Avg eviction batch size: 24 entries
Backpressure events: 12
```

mike: ouch. that 8% growth sounds like fragmentation + small leaks. did you see per-entry lifetimes? could be we don't reclaim stale pages because of fragmentation.

anya: yes, lifetime histogram shows a tail: many entries live >1h even though they haven't been touched for 20-30min. suspect reuse bias: large tenants allocate many medium-sized cache blocks and our free-list compaction is too timid.

cheng: two quick thoughts:
1) per-tenant soft residency quotas with eviction-priority buckets (age-weighted score) — reduces noisy neighbor impact quickly.
2) periodic compaction pass to coalesce small free pages when fragmentation crosses threshold. tradeoff: CPU spike, but can be scheduled during low qps windows.

sre-ops: infra-bot alerted a kvcache_eviction_rate spike at 2026-09-12T14:02:11Z — correlates with a canary that hit long ctx. our SLA had p99 latency blips at that time.

infra-bot: ALERT kvcache_eviction_rate > 50/s for instance r-infer-08 (rule: eviction_rate > 40/s). snapshot_id=20260912-1402

mike: we should also consider tenant-weighted residency accounting: weight by recent token rate (tokens/min) + pinned-residency for model types that legitimately need long ctx. prevents punishing low-traffic tenants.

anya: ran a micro-experiment toggling soft cap=1.2GB/tenant (and strict global cap). results: eviction storms reduced by ~60%, p99 latency improved ~25% for victim tenants. fragmentation unchanged though.

anya: snippet of the eviction scoring function I used in sim:
```
def eviction_score(entry):
  age = now - entry.last_touch
  size = entry.bytes
  token_rate = tenant_tokens_per_min[entry.tenant] + 1
  return (age * 0.6) + (size * 0.3) - (token_rate * 0.1)
```

cheng: simple but pragmatic. i'd shift to an additive quota penalty so big tenants pay more cost when they overshoot sustained usage.

sre-ops: action items?

anya: propose short-term: enable per-tenant soft quota + eviction scoring tweak (age heavy) behind flag; schedule compaction job as experiment; add telemetry: per-tenant residency %, eviction rate, avg entry age, fragmentation ratio. I'll open a follow-up infra ticket with sim artifacts.

mike: +1. also add a perf-regression gate so if compaction causes >10% CPU spike for >5m we auto-roll back.

cheng: i'll drop a patch for the quota bookkeeping and a smoke test to simulate cold ramp.

anya: thanks — putting the sim logs and perf traces in the ticket. ping me if you want the raw heap snapshots. :thumbsup:
